record_note: Wired by hand on 2026-09-19 (commit 3b92406 'quality baseline: gate, contract tests, version pair'), before the kit existed as a git repo — so `revision` is the kit's FIRST PUBLISHED commit, not the exact copy point; do not read it as the tree this repo was copied from. Every copied artifact is deliberately adapted for a Deno 2 + Oak + Postgres app; each reason is below and is also written in INCIDENTS.md. The kit's C++ and Python artifacts (tools/ci.sh, .ci.env.example, templates/*/gate.sh for the other language) were never applicable here and are not listed. Rule that keeps this file true: any commit that edits a copied artifact must update that artifact's repo_sha256 in the same commit.

files.adapted_why: Deno app, not the kit's public/version.js <-> sw.js pair: artifact-identity checks web/version.js APP_VERSION against the ?v= on every local asset reference in every page (and fails when web/ changes without web/version.js); added an env stage and a 'files this branch touches' helper; format tolerates a file already unformatted at HEAD; lint is absolute, no baseline.
Deno-only repo: the C++ branch (exec tools/ci.sh build tests) is deleted, since the whole Deno gate is already seconds and a commit can run all of it.
The C++-only paragraph (clean worktree + pristine checkout of HEAD) is deleted; the Deno gate is already the whole gate and carries its own clean-checkout story.

Seeded from the kit's rule block on 2026-09-19 and carries this repo's own entries plus a 'Deliberate deviations from the AI-DEV-STARTER gate' section; the kit's own 2026-09-19/20 entries are deliberately NOT copied — this file is per-repo history, so a sync must never overwrite it with the kit's.

Filled in for this repo, and named PROJECT-CONTRACT.md rather than CLAUDE.md: CLAUDE.md is a protected agent-instruction name here — creating it opens an approval prompt, and both unattended attempts (2026-09-19, 2026-09-20) were refused, so the contract lives in docs/ until a human runs 'git mv docs/PROJECT-CONTRACT.md CLAUDE.md'.
